review_notes: Both July 14 updates report that five bodies had been recovered from passengers missing after the Simaltal landslide swept the two buses into the Trishuli.
The Panchkot police-post landslide caused major structural damage, but both reports explicitly state there was no human casualty.

The Tinau-3 head-box failure buried and blocked the Butwal-Palpa road. The source describes a landslide with mud and stones; later falling rocks are a continuing risk, not the primary failure mechanism.
The Kushma-2 house landslide killed 70-year-old Rem Bahadur Chalise; his wife was outside the house and no additional deaths are reported.
Two workers were buried when an excavated soil bank collapsed while a drainage track was being dug at Dhumba Lake; this is a worksite soil-bank collapse rather than a natural landslide hazard.
All three reports identify the two three-year-old twins, Sachin and Sandhya Rana Magar, as killed in the Tokha-1 landslide.
The Nilkantha-4 Ranagaun house landslide killed 30-year-old Sharmila Thapa Magar; other impacts in the article are separate flood and road-disruption reports.

The Dhulikhel-8 Chandandanda event is explicitly described as a dry landslide that blocked the highway. Falling stones continued afterward, but the source does not isolate a rockfall as the primary hazard.
The woman was buried while digging soil when an earthen bank collapsed at Bandrang; this is an excavation-related soil-bank collapse, not a natural landslide.
The Kerabari obstruction is reported as a landslide; mud accompanied the failed slope material, but the evidence does not establish a channelized debris-flow process.
The fresh Narayangadh-Muglin landslide at 3 p.m. directly blocked vehicular movement, making road obstruction the supported event type.
The Nagma/Tilagufa-1 update explicitly states that ten people had died and two remained missing; the earlier count of six had been superseded.

The Ata Khola slope failure is consistently described as a landslide from above during road-track work. One excavator driver, Raju Parajuli, was recovered dead while the second person remained missing.
The renewed Gagane Khola landslide again blocked the Karnali Highway, so the supported event type is road obstruction.
The Tulsi Bhanjyang landslide caused roughly 50 metres of the Siddhartha Highway to fail and stopped vehicles, supporting road obstruction.
The obstruction was caused by a massive stone falling from the cliff at Sirubari; the road crew needed a stonebreaker, supporting a discrete rockfall mechanism.
The Runtingadhi-7 fatality occurred when a soil bank collapsed while residents were digging soil near the house; this is an excavation-related bank collapse rather than a natural landslide.
The Siddhababa failure is explicitly reported as a large rain-triggered landslide containing rock, trees and mud; there is no evidence of a distinct channelized debris flow.
A priest was buried when the wall/soil bank and septic-tank edge of a house-construction pit collapsed; this is a construction excavation collapse, not a natural landslide.
The Dhanchaur/Tallopaku landslide buried and killed Govinda Budha Magar and his wife Shyamkala; both bodies were found in the dry-landslide debris.
The Bharpa/Guranse failure is described as a rain-triggered landslide depositing debris and mud on the Mechi Highway; the evidence does not establish a channelized debris-flow event.
The early Lidi update reports that two bodies were visible at the landslide site while 36 people were missing; two deaths are therefore reported in this source snapshot.
The 16-year-old victim died when a soil bank collapsed while she was digging earth near her home; this is an excavation-related soil-bank collapse, with one confirmed death.
The Syangja report explicitly states that two boys, Sameer Shahsin and Anjan Malla, were killed after being buried by the landslide.
The dry landslide near Namdi Khola, Ichchhakamana-6 blocked the Narayangadh-Muglin road; one vehicle occupant was injured.
The Doramba Shailung-3 Lekharka update states the confirmed death toll had reached eight, while two people were still missing.
The Satrakilo obstruction is reported as a mud-laden landslide. The article does not describe a channelized debris-flow process, so landslide is the supported hazard.
The Bhattedanda landslide injured a motorcycle passenger with a fractured leg; the driver was otherwise safe and no death is reported.
Babiran Khatun was struck by a falling boulder while crossing the Turture landslide and was pronounced dead after rescue; one death is confirmed.
The Bhattedanda dry landslide struck a tractor and motorcycle and injured both drivers; no fatality is reported.
Both reports describe the Raghuganga-6 house burial as a landslide, including mud in the failed material; the evidence does not establish a channelized debris flow.
The Ramapur-10 road-maintenance landslide buried the excavator and killed its 24-year-old driver Dhanbir Khadka; the later article is a relief follow-up.
The Timure update explicitly reports four recovered bodies, all container drivers, while five other people remained missing.
